content: The user contributions page provides a detailed list of edits made by a specific user. These pages are project-specific, meaning that a user’s contributions on one project (e.g., Meta) will not display edits made to other projects (e.g., Wikipedia). Reviewing your contributions can help you recall which pages you have worked on and allow you to easily revisit them. Additionally, it enables you to check if subsequent edits have been made to those pages. This functionality allows you to monitor pages even if they are not on your watchlist. You can also access the user contributions pages of other users. This can be useful for understanding how others have contributed, as well as for identifying instances of vandalism, copyright violations, or other issues. To access your own user contributions page, click on My contributions, which is typically displayed at the top of the page or on the left-hand side. If the user does not have a login name, their contributions can be accessed by clicking on their IP address in the Recent Changes or Page History sections, or by entering the IP address in the search box and pressing Go. The user contributions page displays edits in reverse chronological order, from the newest to the oldest. Each edit is shown on a single line, which includes the time and date of the edit, the page name, the edit summary, and other diagnostic information. Key features of the user contributions page include: The username or IP address of the contributor is displayed. You can filter results by selecting a specific namespace (e.g., templates) from a dropdown menu and pressing Go. The time and date of each edit are shown. The (hist) link directs you to the page history, where you can view all edits made to that page. This is useful for checking changes made by others to pages you have worked on. The (diff) link takes you to a diff page, which shows the changes between a specific edit and the current revision. The current revision is displayed below the changes, allowing you to see how the page now appears. The m marker indicates a minor edit, which typically involves small corrections to a page. The page name where the edit occurred is displayed. If the page has been renamed, the current name will be shown. The edit summary reflects the text entered by the user in the edit summary box. If the edit was made to a specific section of the page, the section name appears in grey text, automatically added by the system. The (top) marker signifies that the edit is the current revision of the page. If your last edit does not display (top), it means the page has been changed since your edit. Sysops (administrators) also have a rollback link here for reverting edits. If a user has made only a few edits, all their contributions will fit on one page. For users with extensive contributions, links to additional pages of edits (e.g., Next 100 or Previous 100) will appear. The number of edits displayed per page can be adjusted (e.g., 20, 50, 100, 250, or 500). Certain actions are not shown on the user contributions page, such as: Edits to pages that have been deleted (unless restored). Uploading a new image with the same name as an existing one, thereby replacing it. Deletion or restoration (undeletion) of a page by a sysop. The URL for a user contributions page typically follows this format: `Special:Contributions/XX` or `Special:Contributions&target=XX`, where XX represents the username or IP address. To view contributions on a specific sub-site, adjust the sub-site in the URL. You can also restrict the view to a single namespace by appending the namespace number to the URL (e.g., `Special:Contributions&target=XX&namespace=4`). It is important to note that your contributions are publicly visible to anyone. Please be mindful of this when making edits.
